source.title: Irish News, 2 June 1961, p. 1 ("Nationalists keep control of Limavady Rural Council"); Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1961, p. 9 ("Results: county and rural council elections")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Ballygomartin count read in the Irish News of 2 June 1961 and the News-Letter of the same date; all other returns from the Lisburn Herald (20 May 1961, p. 3).

note: Triennial election of Lisburn Rural District Council, polled Thursday 1 June 1961. Only the Ballygomartin division (Andersonstown, Suffolk and Hannahstown) was reported as contested in the sources read; the other divisions are not listed in the reports consulted. The News-Letter prints the successful candidate as 'Edward L. Boyle' and the loser as standing for the Ratepayers; the Irish News gives 'Eamon Boyle (Ind. Lab.)'. Boyle's majority was 248 with eleven spoiled votes.
